key_insight: A Video Vision Transformer can predict the full time evolution of viscoelastic droplet impacts from only the first 10%–20% of a simulation, capturing spreading and bouncing while saving most of the compute cost.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster surrogate for costly VOF simulations in spray cooling, inkjet printing, and pharmaceutical processing where many parameter sweeps are needed.
method: Uses a ViViT model on VOF volume-fraction fields from droplet impact simulations.
Trains on early-time frames to forecast the remaining droplet dynamics.
Accounts for viscoelastic effects through parameters such as solvent viscosity ratio (β) and Weissenberg number (Wi).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports physically consistent predictions across multiple parameter settings and horizons, with about 80%–90% computational cost reduction relative to full simulations.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the range of training conditions, and robustness to real experimental noise or unseen regimes still needs validation.
paper_title: Prediction of Viscoelastic Droplet Impact Dynamics Using a Vision Transformer-Based Approach
